title: K-ε-GG Peptide Enrichment and Analysis by Tandem Mass Tagging-based Proteomics
author: Harper JW
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.buyunxww
materials: One IP per sample. For one IP: 32 µg of a-K-ε-GG Antibody per 40 µL slurry (Pierce™ Protein A Plus UltraLink™ Resin, Cat. No. 53142) - see below for coupling of antibody to resin. Add the resin to a 15 mL Eppendorf tube.
a. Wash C-18 with 1 mL 100% ACN.
e. Collect flow through and freeze.
d. Load sample (1 drop per second).
b. Equilibrate with 3 mL of 1% FA.
Follow manufacturer’s instructions (Thermo Cat# 84868). Elution used: 17.5% ACN, 20% ACN, 22.5% ACN, 25% ACN, 27.5% ACN and 70% ACN.
Speed vac individual samples to dryness.

The analysis of K-ε-GG peptides by mass spectrometry will depend on the type of instrument/platform used. Typical instrument settings for analysis on a Thermo Fusion Lumos instrument are provided in the following section. Inject 3 µL for each LC–MS/MS analysis using available mass spectrometer with a 120-minute online LC separation.

Seperate peptides on a 100 micromolar (µM) inner diameter microcapillary column packed in house with ~ 35 cm of Accucore150 resin ( 2.6 micromolar (µM) , 150 Å, ThermoFisher Scientific, San Jose, CA) with a gradient consisting of 3%–26% (0-100 min), 26-32% (100-110min) (ACN, 0.1% FA) over a total 02:00:00 run at ~ 400 nL/min .

steps.title: Cell Lysis and Protein Extraction
steps.instruction: Lyse cells and extract proteins using methanol-chloroform precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Lyse cells in 3 mL of lysis buffer and pass through a 21G needle 10 times.
Centrifuge suspensions at 13000 rpm for 10 minutes at 4 °C and collect the supernatant.
Quantify protein lysate concentration and transfer 1 mg of lysates to a clean tube.
Reduce lysates for 20 minutes at room temperature with 5 mM TCEP.
Alkylate cysteine residues with 20 mM Chloroacetamide for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Add 4x volumes of MeOH and vortex.
Spin down at room temperature for 5 minutes at high speed.
Dry protein pellet to remove MeOH traces.
Add 4x volumes of MeOH and vortex.
Carefully remove and discard both aqueous and organic layers.
Spin down at room temperature for 5 minutes at high speed.
Add 3x volume of water and vortex.
Add 1x volume of chloroform and vortex.

steps.title: Protein Digestion
steps.instruction: Perform sequential digestion of proteins using Lys-C and Trypsin.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend protein pellets in 8 M urea and 50 mM EPPS (pH 8.5) buffer.
Dilute samples to 4 M urea with 50 mM EPPS (pH 8.5) and digest at 30 °C for 2 hours with endoproteinase Lys-C (Wako, Japan) at a 1/200 enzyme/protein ratio.
Dilute samples to 1 M urea with 50 mM EPPS (pH 8.5).
Digest with Trypsin (1:100) overnight at 37 °C.
Stop digestion by acidification with 5% (v/v) formic acid (FA) to pH ~2.

steps.title: Peptide Desalting
steps.instruction: Desalt the digested peptides using C18 SepPak cartridges.

substeps.instruction: Subject peptides to C18 SepPak solid-phase extraction (SPE Waters) cartridges and dry down.
Resuspend the desalted peptides in 1.3 mL IAP buffer.

steps.title: Antibody Preparation and Cross-linking
steps.instruction: Prepare the anti-K-ε-GG antibody beads via DMP cross-linking.

substeps.instruction: Wash 3x with PBS and centrifuge for 1 minute at 1000 x g.
Add the a-K-ε-GG Antibody and add PBS to reach a total volume of 10 mL in a 15 mL tube.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with gentle rotation.
Wash the anti-K-ε-GG Antibody coupled beads 3x with 3 mL 100 mM sodium borate, pH 9.0.
Resuspend the beads in 3 mL of 20 mM DMP in 100 mM sodium borate (pH 9.0) and incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes with a gentle end-over-end rotator.
Stop the reaction by washing the beads 2x with 3 mL of antibody blocking buffer (200 mM ethanolamine pH 8.0).
Resuspend in 3 mL of Antibody blocking buffer and incubate for 2 hours at 4 °C with gentle rotation.
Wash the cross-linked antibody 3x with 3 mL IAP buffer.

steps.title: K-ε-GG Peptide Immunoprecipitation (IP)
steps.instruction: Enrich K-ε-GG peptides using the prepared cross-linked antibody beads.

substeps.instruction: Add each sample to a clean 2 mL Eppendorf tube containing 40 µL slurry of cross-linked anti-K-ε-GG Antibody resin.
Incubate the IPs for 2 hours at 4 °C with gentle end-over-end rotation.
Centrifuge each IP at 2000 x g for 2 minutes, remove the supernatant, and store supernatant at -80 °C.
Wash the beads 3x with 2 mL of IAP buffer, followed by a wash with 2 mL PBS.
Elute K-ε-GG peptides by adding 75 µL of elution solution (0.15% TFA), tapping the tube bottom, and letting it stand at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Repeat the elution step and combine both eluates.
Dry down in speedvac.

steps.title: First C-18 Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform initial C-18 cleanup of the eluted peptides.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend samples in 5% FA, 5% ACN.
Wash with 3 mL of 1% FA/5% ACN.
Elute with 2 x 500 µL 75% ACN/1% FA.
Dry down in speedvac.

steps.title: TMT Labeling
steps.instruction: Label the enriched peptides with TMT reagents.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the peptide pellet in 50 µL of 200 mM EPPS (pH 8.2) containing 20% ACN.
Add 3 µL - 4 µL of the TMT reagent to each sample.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Stop the reaction with 4 µL of 5% hydroxylamine.

steps.title: Second C-18 Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform a second C-18 cleanup after TMT labeling.

substeps.instruction: Combine samples, acidify with 5% FA, and speed-vac to dryness (gel-like consistency).
Resuspend samples in 5% FA, 5% ACN.
Wash with 3 mL of 1% FA/5% ACN.
Elute with 2 x 500 µL 75% ACN/1% FA.
Dry down in speedvac.

steps.title: Fractionation and Stage-Tip Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform final C18-based stage-tip cleanup on six fractions.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend samples in 5% FA, 5% ACN.
For each of the six fractions, perform the following stage-tip steps:
Wash C-18 with 50 µL 100% ACN; centrifuge at 2000 x g for 2 minutes at room temperature and discard flowthrough.
Equilibrate with 50 µL of 1% FA; centrifuge at 2000 x g for 2 minutes at room temperature and discard flowthrough.
Load sample; centrifuge at 1500 x g for 4 minutes at room temperature.
Wash with 50 µL of 1% FA/5% ACN; centrifuge at 2000 x g for 2 minutes at room temperature and discard flowthrough.
Elute with 1 x 50 µL 75% ACN/% FA into a mass-spec vial; centrifuge at 2000 x g for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Dry down in speedvac.
Resuspend in 10 µL 5% FA, 5% ACN.

steps.title: Mass Spectrometry Data Acquisition
steps.instruction: Collect MS data using an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer and Proxeon EASY-nLC1200 pump.

substeps.instruction: Load 1/3 of each fraction onto the column using the Multi-Notch MS3-based TMT method.
MS1 scan: Orbitrap analysis; resolution 120,000 at 200 Th; mass range 400-1250 m/z; AGC target 1×10^6; max injection time 100 ms.
MS2 analysis: Select precursors using Top 4 sec method; quadrupole Orbitrap analysis; AGC 1×10^5; isolation window 0.7 Th; NCE 35; max injection time 300 ms; resolution 7,500 at 200 Th.
Use monoisotopic peak assignment and exclude previously interrogated precursors using a dynamic window (120 s ± 7 ppm).
Select only precursors with a charge state between 3 and 6 for downstream analysis.
SPS MS3 scan: Collect on the top 10 most intense ions in the MS2 spectrum.
MS3 fragmentation: High energy collision-induced dissociation (HCD); Orbitrap analysis; NCE 65; AGC 2×10^5; max injection time 500 ms; resolution 50,000 at 200 Th.

steps.title: Proteomic Data Analysis
steps.instruction: Process raw MS data to identify proteins and quantify TMT ratios.

substeps.instruction: Search raw data against UniProt human protein database.
Parameters: Up to 3 missed cleavages for trypsin/LysC; Fixed modifications: Carbamidomethyl (C), TMT (N-term peptide and K); Variable modifications: Oxidation (M) and di-glycine (K).
Extract signal to noise intensity values of each TMT reporter and identified proteins.
Calculate the ratio of each condition to the control sample’s intensity.
